concerns.text: T000 explicitly documents a 'Scope Reduction' from the spec's 'Human Subject Study' to a 'Deterministic Simulation'. This is a silent weakening of FR-001/FR-003 which mandate real participant interaction data. The task list accepts this drift without a corresponding spec amendment, violating the constraint that tasks must not relax what the spec demands.

These tasks implement simulated participant interactions (T015-base: 'simulate participant interaction logs') instead of the real data collection required by FR-003 and US-1. The spec requires recording 'participant interaction data' from 'graduate-level software engineering students', but the tasks only generate synthetic data with 'injected effect sizes', rendering the success criteria (SC-001, SC-002) untestable against real human behavior.

FR-002 requires the system to 'automatically fall back to the rule-based summary' during the study execution when LLM generation fails. T015-fallback-check implements a post-hoc check that 'generates the rule-based summary on-the-fly' for missing entries in the log. This is a semantic weakening: the spec requires real-time fallback during the interaction, whereas the task implements a batch repair step after the fact, failing to satisfy the real-time constraint of the FR.

T014-real is marked [Manual] and moved to Phase 0, explicitly excluded from CI. While the Plan acknowledges this, the Spec (FR-002) mandates the system 'MUST generate' LLM summaries with fallback. By making the real generation a manual offline step, the tasks effectively remove the 'automatic' nature of the requirement from the automated pipeline, creating a gap where the system cannot satisfy FR-002 in its primary execution mode (CI) without manual intervention.
